article_title: Participation And performance In 8.02x Electricity And Magnetism: The First Physics MOOC From MITx
citation: Saif Rayyan, Daniel T. Seaton, John Belcher, David E. Pritchard, Isaac Chuang. (2013). Participation And performance In 8.02x Electricity And Magnetism: The First Physics MOOC From MITx. arXiv. https://arxiv.org/abs/1310.3173
title: 8.02x: MITx's first introductory physics MOOC on the edX platform (Spring 2013)
description: 8.02x is a Massive Open Online Course offered through edX in Spring 2013, centered on recorded video lectures of MIT's Introductory Physics II broken into roughly 5-10 segments with interspersed machine-graded multiple choice questions. Other components include "machine graded weekly homework sets", TEAL simulations with concept questions, videotaped problem solving sessions, an e-Textbook, three midterm exams and a final exam, and a threaded discussion board. Certification is granted for scores greater than 60%.
constraints: The course ran for 16 weeks from February 2013 to June 2013, equivalent in length to a semester long course at MIT
target_learners: Worldwide adult learners of introductory physics, including college-aged students and advanced degree holders
target_learning_goals: Introductory electricity and magnetism (Introductory Physics II)
examples: Lectures were broken into roughly 5-10 segments with machine graded multiple choice questions worth 5% of the grade; homework 18%, simulations 2%, midterms 15% each, final 30%
